% Written by `lab paper game-rating`; do not edit by hand.
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{lL}
\toprule
Feature & Description \\
\midrule
\texttt{loss\_mean} & The mean win probability lost by the player's moves, in percentage points. \\
\texttt{loss\_median} & The median win probability lost by the player's moves, in percentage points. \\
\texttt{loss\_worst} & The win probability lost by the player's most costly move, in percentage points. \\
\texttt{loss\_over\_5} & The share of the player's moves that lost more than 5 percentage points of win probability. \\
\texttt{loss\_over\_10} & The share of the player's moves that lost more than 10 percentage points of win probability. \\
\texttt{loss\_over\_20} & The share of the player's moves that lost more than 20 percentage points of win probability. \\
\texttt{win\_before\_mean} & The player's win probability before each of the moves, averaged over the moves, in percent. \\
\texttt{spent\_mean} & The mean time the player spent on a move, in seconds. \\
\texttt{spent\_median} & The median time the player spent on a move, in seconds. \\
\texttt{spent\_longest} & The longest time the player spent on one move, in seconds. \\
\texttt{spent\_under\_2} & The share of the player's moves that took less than 2 seconds. \\
\texttt{spent\_over\_30} & The share of the player's moves that took more than 30 seconds. \\
\texttt{clock\_lowest} & The lowest time on the player's clock before any of the moves, in seconds. \\
\texttt{clock\_used} & The share of the initial time that had elapsed before the last of the moves; an increment can make it negative. \\
\texttt{legal\_moves\_mean} & The number of legal moves the player had, averaged over the moves. \\
\texttt{capture\_share} & The share of the player's moves that were captures. \\
\texttt{check\_share} & The share of the player's moves that gave check. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
